subdivision_of_building: existing slab and timber garden shelter in southwest corner of the former pumping station grounds
description: Demolition of existing timber shelter; construction and temporary use of a timber sauna within the grounds of the Grade II* listed former pumping station (The Castle Climbing Centre)
decision_conditions:
<p>The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.</p><p>REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).</p><p>
</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The development hereby permitted shall be for a limited period only and shall be removed from the site no later than 5 years from the implementation date of the development.</span></p><p>REASON: In the interests of aligning with the terms of the development as proposed.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Prior to the first use of the sauna, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority showing the location of the external ventilation system. The external vent shall be positioned on the elevation furthest from the retained trees and oriented to discharge upward and away from trees. Any air discharged from the sauna ventilation system shall not exceed 50 °C at the terminal face. The details as approved shall endure for the duration of the operation.</span></p><p>REASON: In the interests of preserving protected bat species in Hackney, in line with the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Prior to the first use of the sauna, an External Lighting Scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall be designed and implemented in accordance with the Bat Conservation Trust guidelines and must be sensitive to wildlife. The lighting design should ensure that:&nbsp;</span></p><ul style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:0;padding-inline-start:48px;"><li dir="ltr" style="list-style-type: disc; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; margin-left: 36pt;" aria-level="1"><p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;" role="presentation"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Harsh lighting is minimised to avoid making habitats (including the green roof) unfavourable to local species, particularly bats and other nocturnal wildlife.</span></p></li><li dir="ltr" style="list-style-type: disc; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; margin-left: 36pt;" aria-level="1"><p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;" role="presentation"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The use of low-intensity lighting is prioritised, ensuring that any light sources do not directly illuminate bat roosts, foraging areas, trees and vegetation or flight paths.&nbsp;</span></p></li><li dir="ltr" style="list-style-type: disc; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; margin-left: 36pt;" aria-level="1"><p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;" role="presentation"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">All lighting fixtures are shielded or directed to limit light pollution and to maintain dark corridors that are critical for bat and wildlife movement.&nbsp;</span></p></li></ul><p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The approved lighting scheme shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the development and maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved details.</span></p><p>REASON: To protect local wildlife, particularly bats, from the negative impacts of artificial lighting, and to ensure compliance with the Bat Conservation Trust guidelines.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The sauna shall only be open between the hours of 8am - 10pm on weekdays, 9am - 8pm on weekends. The lighting at the facility shall be turned off outside these operational hours.&nbsp;</span></p><p>REASON: To protect the amenity of nearby occupiers and reduce the potential for antisocial behaviour.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Prior to the first use of the sauna, a management plan for the sauna including management responsibilities and customer management measures to ensure the operation does not result in undue noise and disturbance shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The measures set out in the approved plan shall be complied with in full, with effect from commencement of use of the sauna hereby approved.&nbsp;</span></p><p>REASON: To protect the amenity of nearby occupiers and reduce the potential for antisocial behaviour.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Light from the luminaires shall not exceed 10 EV (lux) within suburban surroundings (or 25 EV (lux) within urban surroundings) when measured at any residential or light sensitive window overlooking the development. All luminaries shall be oriented and designed in such a way to minimise light spillage beyond the boundary and prevent glare into the windows of residential or light sensitive properties overlooking the development. The applicant must submit light contour maps to show how the proposed lighting scheme will impact on the surrounding residents. This scheme shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval prior to installing the lights.</span></p><p>REASON: In the interests of protecting residential amenities.&nbsp;</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The works hereby approved shall not be carried out unless in accordance with the approved Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan by Ryan Hurdle of R&amp;G dated 27.04.2026 ref. P169-01. Any surfacing within the Root Protection Areas (RPAs) of retained trees must be installed and maintained in line with the approved AMS using a ‘no-dig’ method as outlined within the report.</span></p><p>REASON: To safeguard existing trees in the interests of visual amenity.&nbsp; </p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">All new underground utility apparatus, including drainage, shall be routed and installed outside the Root Protection Area(s) (RPAs) shown on the approved drawings. Should it not be feasible to route new underground utility apparatus outside the RPAs of retained trees, trenchless insertion methods (as detailed in BS 5837:2012, Table 3) shall be employed for their installation within the RPAs, with entry and retrieval pits sited outside the RPAs. No other new underground utilities shall be installed within the RPAs of retained trees without prior written consent from the Local Planning Authority (LPA). Any such works, if permitted, shall be carried out in strict accordance with the principles of BS 5837:2012 "Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations" and the National Joint Utilities Group Guidelines for the planning, installation and maintenance of utility apparatus in proximity to trees, Volume 4, Issue 2 (2007) (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this standard).</span></p><p>REASON: To safeguard existing tree(s) in the interests of visual amenity and long-term tree health.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height:1.38;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification and a drainage layout of the living roof (minimum substrate depth of 100mm excluding the vegetative mat, and suitable planting mix) and attenuation tank shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume.</span></p><p>REASON: To ensure the development incorporates appropriate sustainable drainage measures, manages surface water effectively, and does not increase flood risk on or off site. </p>

<p>The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.<br></p>
